climate: Few classic table-wine grapes keep their freshness in heat like this. It suits fortified wine, table grapes and raisins.
Most rain falls while the vines grow. Damp leaves invite mildew and rot, so growers spray more and pick carefully.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity. River deposits are a mix of gravel, sand and silt. They are often fertile, so vines can grow vigorously.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
